translation_notes: `for type_ in value: g.add((subject, RDF.type, URIRef(type_)))` -> `for @bindings in ({"t": rdflib.URIRef(type_)} for type_ in value): +{ {subject} a ?t }` -- the one loop in this region that is genuinely row-shaped (each iteration writes exactly one triple, no branching on the loop item itself), so it is the clean match for the stratum's target construction. Predicate `a`/rdf:type is fixed; only the object varies per row, carried as `?t`.

the second loop (`for obj in value: ... g.add((subject, URIRef(key), obj))`) is NOT recast with @bindings: `obj` is produced by branching that differs in KIND, not just value -- @list (raise or continue), @id vs @value, and a recursive call to _insert_resource itself that has the side effect of writing into `g` while the binding would be computed. Wrapping that in a bindings-generator would either move side effects out of order or force the branches into a helper function, i.e. restructure control flow to fit the idiom rather than translate it. Kept as +{ } with plain {expr} interpolation, one 1:1 swap for each `g.add`, both branches unmerged as in the source.

`@graph g` designates the existing `g` parameter as current (rather than the mechanical `g += g{ ... }` a first pass produced): this is the more specific construction per INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2 for a graph passed in as an object, not created locally.
no context shim needed: the region only imports json, typing.Any and rdflib, all available as-is.

Correction : pour un objet imbriqué à une seule propriété (ni @id, ni @value, ni @list), l'original lève AssertionError (g.add exige un terme rdflib) alors que +{ {subject} {rdflib.URIRef(key)} {obj} } écrivait en silence Literal(str(dict)) ; le pilote renforcé (RESOURCE_4 et RESOURCE_5) l'a fait échouer, et ce cas existe dans le dépôt (jsonld_to_graph appelle _insert_resource sur la sortie de jsonld.expand). La branche len(obj) == 1 garde donc `g.add` pour l'objet encore dict, et +{ } pour le reste ; la région n'est plus entièrement en +{ }.

repair.driver: quatre ressources ajoutées : RESOURCE_3 (@list non vide, la branche raise Exception("@list not supported"), avec un objet écrit avant), RESOURCE_4 (objet imbriqué à une seule propriété {'http://e/q': [{'@value': 'v'}]}, atteint dans le dépôt par jsonld_to_graph), RESOURCE_5 (le même, mêlé à des termes écrits avant et à un @type), RESOURCE_6 (objet à @id + autre propriété = récursion, objet à @id + @value = le @value l'emporte) ; la docstring périmée sur la @list est remplacée.
mutants_killed: retrait de la garde isinstance(obj, dict) (la traduction d'origine, rejetée par RESOURCE_4 et RESOURCE_5)
repair.remaining: Jugements non traités : la classification directly-expressible tient-elle, maintenant que la branche len(obj) == 1 garde un `g.add` en repli ? (classification-doubt) ; la boucle des types en `for @bindings in ({"t": …} for …)` au lieu de `for type_ in value: +{ {subject} a {rdflib.URIRef(type_)} }` (classification-doubt).

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `if key == '@id': continue` folds into `elif key != '@id'`; the `@list` test becomes `len(obj) == 1 and '@list' in obj` with a bare `continue` (the `else: continue` goes); the two object branches (len 1 / other) merge into one chain `@value` -> Literal, len != 1 -> recursion, `@id` -> URIRef, else the dict as is, followed by one shared g.add: a len-1 dict cannot hold both @id and @value, so the order of the two tests does not matter, and the same chain gives the same exceptions on str and list items; `len(obj['@list']) > 0` is kept (truthiness would not raise on a non-sized value). The try/except/print/raise is unchanged; the TODO comment block is kept.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph g`, `+{ {subject} a f<{type_}> }` in a plain loop (no @bindings generator, unlike the translation), `f<…>` for the three URIRef calls, one `+{ {subject} f<{key}> {obj} }` after the chain.

Cost of the island, not a restructuring to carry back: the len-1 dict that is neither @id, @value nor @list must still reach rdflib's AssertionError, which `+{ }` would turn into a Literal; optimized.ldpy therefore gives the chain an explicit `else:` that keeps `g.add` and `continue`s. Python needs no such branch.
rdflib.Literal(obj['@value']) is kept as a call: obj is then interpolated whole, and a null @value gives Literal('None') where a bare interpolation raises.
header_optimization_notes: Nothing unused in the header on either side (json, Any and rdflib are all read): optimized_header.py and optimized_header.ldpy are copies of the optimized files.
